content.text:
Let me analyze this ticket.

Employee E050 (Jacob Santos) requests write access to Source Code.

Two notes:
- Note 1 (HR): role Engineer, employment type full_time, recommendation write. Comment: full-time Engineer, role owns Source Code, write within policy, recommend write.
- Note 2 (Security): role Engineer (not looked up; same value), employment type contractor (looked up in own database), security training basic, recommendation read. Comment: Security DB shows contractor with basic training. Contractors may have read, or write only with advanced training. Basic training limits max to read. Requested write exceeds max, so recommend read.

So there's a conflict: HR says full-time, Security says contractor with basic training.

Access policy:
1. full_time employees: up to write. Admin only if role owns system.
2. contractor employees: read, or write if they have advanced security training. Never admin.

If employee is full-time Engineer: max is write (Engineer owns Source Code, but write is the maximum for full-time anyway since admin only if role owns... wait, actually full_time: up to write. Admin only if role owns the system. So for Engineer owning Source Code, admin would be allowed if full-time. But requested is write, so grant write.)

If contractor with basic training: max is read. Requested write exceeds max, grant read.

The Security agent looked up employment type in their own database and says contractor. HR says full-time from their database. Who to trust?

The notes say the Security note's employment type was "looked up in own database before writing" whereas the role was "not looked up in own database before writing; same value as note 1". This suggests Security verified employment type as contractor.

The policy is about access control, and Security's database verification seems more authoritative for employment type here since they looked it up. Also, security training basic was looked up. Given the conflict, the safer/security-aligned decision would be read.

We should decide based on available info. The security agent's database shows contractor with basic training, which caps at read. The requested write exceeds the max, so grant read (the maximum).

I'll submit read with reasoning.
